external_entities.name: duty engineer
external_entities.description: An engineer who opens the dispatch console in a browser.
external_entities.source_excerpt: Duty engineers sit on the corporate network. They open the dispatch console in their browser.

external_entities.name: scheduling partner
external_entities.description: Another company that publishes tomorrow's planned work.
external_entities.source_excerpt: A scheduling partner, which is another company, publishes tomorrow's planned work.

processes.name: corporate web host
processes.description: The corporate web host serves the dispatch console.
processes.source_excerpt: our corporate web host serves it

processes.name: dispatch console
processes.description: A single-page JavaScript app opened by duty engineers in their browser.
processes.source_excerpt: The console is a single-page JavaScript app
processes.notes: Nobody wrote down how an engineer signs in to it. The console and the API are served from different origins.

processes.name: dispatch API
processes.description: The API called by the dispatch console and schedule importer; it runs in the production control plane.
processes.source_excerpt: The dispatch API runs in the production control plane.
processes.notes: The control plane is not reachable from the internet. CORS origins and credential handling are undocumented.

processes.name: schedule importer
processes.description: A process on the corporate network that pulls and parses the scheduling partner's SOAP feed, archives downloaded documents, and posts parsed work orders to the dispatch API.
processes.source_excerpt: Our schedule importer runs on the corporate network.
processes.notes: The partner's authentication of the importer and the importer's authentication of the partner are undocumented. The API token was issued when the importer was built and has not been rotated.

data_stores.name: dispatch database
data_stores.description: A database holding job orders, crew names, crew mobile numbers, and the token or session that created each job order.
data_stores.source_excerpt: That database holds the job orders, the crew names and the crew mobile numbers.
data_stores.notes: Every job order carries the token or the session that created it, and nothing about the person behind that token. Protection at rest is undocumented.

data_stores.name: schedule archive
data_stores.description: A folder on the corporate file store containing each document downloaded from the scheduling partner.
data_stores.source_excerpt: It writes each document it downloads into the schedule archive, a folder on the corporate file store.

data_flows.name: duty engineer opens dispatch console
data_flows.description: A duty engineer opens the dispatch console in a browser.
data_flows.source_excerpt: They open the dispatch console in their browser.
data_flows.notes: The engineer's sign-in method is undocumented.

data_flows.name: corporate web host serves dispatch console
data_flows.description: The corporate web host serves the dispatch console application.
data_flows.source_excerpt: our corporate web host serves it

data_flows.name: dispatch console calls dispatch API
data_flows.description: The dispatch console calls the dispatch API cross-origin.
data_flows.source_excerpt: The console calls the dispatch API.
data_flows.notes: The API answers the console cross-origin. Allowed origins and whether credentials are allowed were not recorded.

data_flows.name: dispatch console opens WebSocket to dispatch API
data_flows.description: The dispatch console opens and holds a WebSocket to the dispatch API for live job status.
data_flows.source_excerpt: The console also opens a WebSocket to the dispatch API and holds it open for live job status.
data_flows.notes: Whether the socket uses TLS, whether its handshake is authenticated, and whether it rechecks the engineer's session are undocumented.

data_flows.name: dispatch API reads and writes dispatch database
data_flows.description: The dispatch API reads and writes the dispatch database.
data_flows.source_excerpt: The dispatch API reads and writes the dispatch database.
data_flows.data_description: job orders, crew names, crew mobile numbers, and creating token or session

data_flows.name: schedule importer pulls scheduling partner feed
data_flows.description: Every hour, the schedule importer pulls the scheduling partner's SOAP feed over HTTPS.
data_flows.source_excerpt: Every hour it pulls the partner's SOAP feed over HTTPS
data_flows.notes: Nothing was written down about how the partner identifies the importer, or how the importer identifies the partner.

data_flows.name: schedule importer writes schedule archive
data_flows.description: The schedule importer writes each downloaded document into the schedule archive.
data_flows.source_excerpt: It writes each document it downloads into the schedule archive
data_flows.data_description: downloaded XML documents containing planned work

data_flows.name: schedule importer posts work orders to dispatch API
data_flows.description: The importer posts parsed work orders to the dispatch API using an API token.
data_flows.source_excerpt: The importer then posts the parsed work orders to the same dispatch API the console calls. It presents an API token.
data_flows.notes: The token was issued when the importer was built and nobody has rotated it since.

trust_boundaries.name: corporate network
trust_boundaries.description: The corporate network containing duty engineers, the corporate web host, the schedule importer, and the schedule archive.
trust_boundaries.source_excerpt: Duty engineers sit on the corporate network.

trust_boundaries.name: production control plane
trust_boundaries.description: The same-company, same-staff zone holding the live estate, where an account can move a crew and change the work a depot does that day.
trust_boundaries.source_excerpt: The control plane is the same company and the same staff, but it is the zone that holds the live estate
trust_boundaries.notes: A corporate laptop holds none of the control-plane rights. The control plane is not reachable from the internet.

trust_boundaries.name: scheduling partner
trust_boundaries.description: A zone controlled by the scheduling partner, which is another company.
trust_boundaries.source_excerpt: A scheduling partner, which is another company

assumptions.assumption: The dispatch console is internal because it is used by engineers on the corporate network.
assumptions.basis: The text says duty engineers sit on the corporate network and open the console there.

assumptions.assumption: The dispatch console presents a web interface.
assumptions.basis: The text describes it as a browser-based single-page JavaScript app.

assumptions.assumption: The dispatch API is internal because the control plane is not reachable from the internet.
assumptions.basis: The text explicitly says the control plane is not reachable from the internet.

assumptions.assumption: The dispatch API presents a web interface.
assumptions.basis: The text names it as an API called by a browser console and describes cross-origin API responses.

assumptions.assumption: The schedule importer is a non-web process.
assumptions.basis: The text describes it as an hourly importer that pulls a SOAP feed, parses XML, archives documents, and posts work orders.

assumptions.assumption: The schedule importer is internal because it runs on the corporate network.
assumptions.basis: The text explicitly says the schedule importer runs on the corporate network.

assumptions.assumption: The dispatch database is in the production control plane.
assumptions.basis: The database is the dispatch API's backing store, and the API is stated to run in the production control plane.

assumptions.assumption: The schedule archive is in the corporate network.
assumptions.basis: The archive is a folder on the corporate file store, while the importer and corporate file store are described in the corporate-network context.

assumptions.assumption: The dispatch database is confidential because it contains crew mobile numbers and tokens or sessions.
assumptions.basis: The text states that the database holds crew mobile numbers and that every job order carries the token or session that created it.
